data.name: Manohar
data.gender_notes: Manohar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manohar is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'manas' which means mind or desire. The name is associated with the Hindu god Manavaraha or Manasa, who is believed to control the mind, emotions, and desires. Manohar is a powerful name that evokes a sense of inner strength, wisdom, and self-control. The name Manohar carries the meaning “God of Mind or Desire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manohar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of mind or desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the power to control one's mind and emotions.
data.etymology: Manohar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Mind or Desire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manohar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Manohar has been used extensively in Hindu literature, mythology, and folklore. It evokes a sense of reverence and respect within the Hindu community, especially in India and Nepal. In Hindu culture, the name is often associated with divine wisdom, intellect, and the ability to discern between right and wrong. It is also believed to bring good luck and fortune to the bearer of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Manohar represents the divine power that resides within each individual's mind. It reminds us of the importance of controlling our thoughts and desires and maintaining inner peace and harmony. The name also serves as a reminder of the Hindu belief in the interconnectedness of all things, as the mind is believed to be the bridge between the individual soul and the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manohar's name symbolizes the one who captivates the heart with wisdom and knowledge, embodiment of divine intellect. A beacon of truth and inner beauty, Manohar's essence is to inspire and enlighten.

historical_references.reference: Manohar was a general in the army of King Prithviraj Chauhan during the 12th century. He is best known for his exploits in the Battle of Tarain (1192 AD) against Mohammed Ghori, in which Prithviraj was defeated and captured.

historical_references.reference: Manohar is also the name of one of the 27 stars in the Indian lunar mansion (Nakshatra) called 'Mrigasira'. This star was believed to be associated with the god Agni, the god of fire.
